Build HyQ (Hypothetical Queries) RAG alongside the existing naive RAG. Match the professor's reference pattern from https://github.com/rsm-genai-2026/customer-ticket-process-rag

CRITICAL RULES:
- No em dashes or any dashes in code or commits
- Git author: merna, email msaad@ucsd.edu
- No co author lines
- Work on a new branch called "add-hyq-rag"
- Do NOT touch main until tests pass

STEP 1: Create the branch
git checkout -b add-hyq-rag

STEP 2: Study the existing naive RAG

Look at ai_engine/rag/ to understand the current setup:
ls ai_engine/rag/
cat ai_engine/rag/build_index.py
cat ai_engine/rag/retrieval.py
ls ai_engine/rag/knowledge_base/
ls ai_engine/rag/index/

Note the chunking strategy, embedding model, and index format.

STEP 3: Design the HyQ pipeline

For each chunk in the existing 78 chunks:
a) Call Claude (via TritonAI) with a prompt like:
   "You are generating hypothetical questions that a user might ask which this text chunk could answer. Generate 3 to 5 questions. Be specific. Output JSON array of question strings only, no preamble."
   Pass the chunk text as user input.
b) Parse the JSON response to get an array of questions
c) Embed each question using the same sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 model
d) Store the embedding alongside metadata: source_doc_id, chunk_id, original_chunk_text, generated_question

The HyQ index stores BOTH the original chunk embeddings AND the question embeddings. When retrieving, the system searches both, returns the underlying chunks.

STEP 4: Build the HyQ index

Create ai_engine/rag/hyq/ directory.

Create ai_engine/rag/hyq/build_hyq_index.py:
- Loads the existing chunks from ai_engine/rag/index/chunks.json
- For each chunk, calls Claude to generate 3 to 5 hypothetical questions
- Builds a FAISS IndexFlatIP with embeddings of both chunks AND their generated questions
- Saves the index to ai_engine/rag/hyq/index.faiss
- Saves the chunk+question metadata to ai_engine/rag/hyq/chunks_with_questions.json
- Print pro
